title: Philly Wins the Revenge Game, JMoney Finally Wins Anything, and Kai Benches 61 Points
dek: Three teams sit at 4-1 after Team Pillbert flattened the Dawgs, Counting or not Counting GV crushed the rookie for its first win, and No Banner only HULK's title odds climbed to 55%.
body: The revenge game had a clear winner, and it wasn't the guys seeking revenge. Alan's Team Pillbert beat Mekhi's Dawgs 143.66 to 108.44, the week's top score, behind Jahmyr Gibbs going for 35.2 on a 24.57 projection. Here's the twist: Kai's new arrivals actually won the trade-within-the-game, with Davante Adams posting 19.6 and Ashton Jeanty 9.2, a combined 28.8, while Justin Jefferson gave Philly 15.8 in his debut. The scoreboard didn't care one bit. Team Pillbert has won four straight, sits at 4-1, and kept tinkering anyway, adding Keon Coleman and Odell Beckham Jr. and picking up Joe Mixon just long enough to drop him again.

Mekhi's real opponent was his own lineup screen. Tyler Shough started at quarterback and finished at negative 0.16 on a 16.51 projection, while Jayden Daniels sat on the Dawgs bench putting up 32.26. Christian Watson added 29.3 more from the pine, so Kai left 61.56 points in storage. To be fair to the man, the Daniels swap alone would have left him 2.8 points short, but it's hard to beat a 4-1 team when your quarterback finishes below zero. The wire never stops for Kai, though: he grabbed Malik Nabers for TreVeyon Henderson, swapped the Ravens D/ST for the Bengals, and replaced Harrison Mevis with Will Reichard.

Meanwhile, JMoney finally got off the schneid, and he did it in style. Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV beat Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN 119.68 to 69.14 as a 43% underdog, a 50.54-point blowout. The headliner was Isaiah Likely, who posted 26.9 in his first start after arriving from Philly, and the other two pieces of that deal, Emeka Egbuka (14.2) and Denzel Boston (12.1), scored from the bench. That came despite Jeremiyah Love managing 2.2 on a 13.06 projection. After four weeks of sour notes, the band finally got to play the fight song.

It was a rough afternoon for Zilgit. Ghostu-Spider SZN's 69.14 was the lowest score of the week by more than 30 points, and the cruelest part is that her big move from last week worked: Jared Goff, the quarterback she picked up, delivered 28.94 on a 19.41 projection. The rest of the lineup combined for 40.2. She falls to 2-3 with a 10% shot at the playoffs, and the rookie now has her first real lesson in how quickly a hot streak can cool off.

Sonny kept pace at the top. The Horse is Hea beat Kaushal's Habibsters 137.6 to 118.34 as a slight underdog, powered by Bucky Irving's 30.5 on a 13.97 projection, and the commish's title odds jumped from 11% to 18%. Habib got 29.2 from Puka Nacua, but CeeDee Lamb went from last week's 32.8 to 1.9 on a 15.46 projection, which is about as fast as a man can go from hero to footnote. Kaushal now owns the league's fourth-highest point total at 577.4 and a 1-4 record, a combination that should be investigated. Sonny also swapped Tony Pollard for Emanuel Wilson, and the newest entry on the trade ledger has him sending Chuba Hubbard and DeVonta Smith to Alan for George Pickens and Ollie Gordon II.

And then there's Brucie. No Banner only HULK handled Randy's The fumblers 134 to 99.64, with Josh Allen throwing up 30.5 on a 19.9 projection while Matthew Stafford's 27.32 sat on the bench, a mistake only the league's richest team can shrug off. Ramon now leads the league with 695 points, 70.5 more than anyone else, and his title odds jumped from 41% to 55%. Randy got a monster 33.8 from Jaylen Warren on a 15.86 projection and still lost by 34, his second straight defeat, and his title odds cratered from 14% to 4%. His waiver activity was a round trip worth framing: he dropped Trevor Lawrence for Deshaun Watson, then dropped Watson and picked Lawrence back up, with Romeo Doubs, Matt Gay, and the Raiders D/ST joining while Courtland Sutton and Tyler Loop hit the street.

The standings: No Banner only HULK, Team Pillbert, and The Horse is Hea are all 4-1, The fumblers are 3-2 with 48% playoff odds, Ghostu-Spider SZN is 2-3, and Habibsters, Dawgs, and Counting or not Counting GV sit at 1-4. Oddly, Team Pillbert's title odds read 16%, down from 21% a week ago despite a 35-point win, and Sonny has slipped past him at 18%. Week 6's main event is The Horse is Hea against No Banner only HULK, the commish taking his shot at the 55% favorite. Philly faces Randy in a meeting of former trade partners, Zoe and Kai both need a win to stay in the hunt, and Habib gets JMoney, who suddenly knows what winning feels like.

social.author: Pillbert Nation
social.text: Four straight. 143.66. Gibbs 35.2. Yes, Adams and Jeanty outscored Jefferson. No, we will not be taking questions about that. Check the standings.

social.author: Dawgs Den
social.text: Shough: -0.16. Daniels on the bench: 32.26. Watson on the bench: 29.3. We are not okay. We are, however, adding Malik Nabers.

social.author: GV Counting Club
social.text: Wins counted: 1. Margin counted: 50.54. Isaiah Likely counted: 26.9. We have finally found a number we love.

social.author: Spider SZN Fan Club
social.text: Goff gave us 28.94 exactly like we planned. The other guys gave us 40.2 combined. We are filing a complaint with the cheese curd committee.

social.author: HULK Smash Society
social.text: 695 points. 55% title odds. Stafford's 27 on the bench and we still won by 34. Commish, see you Sunday. Bring your best lineup, we'll bring ours. Probably.

social.author: Fumblers Faithful
social.text: Jaylen Warren drops 33.8 and we lose by 34. Also Trevor Lawrence went on a brief vacation and came right back. Nobody asked how our week was.

social.author: Waiver Wire Wendy
social.text: Randy's transaction log this week reads like a man arguing with himself and losing both sides. Lawrence out, Watson in, Watson out, Lawrence in. Character development.

social.author: Habib Hive
social.text: CeeDee last week: 32.8. CeeDee this week: 1.9. 577.4 points and 1-4. Two rings in the case and no luck in the tank.

social.author: The Stable Report
social.text: Bucky Irving 30.5. Odds 11% to 18%. Three teams at 4-1 and the commish gets the big one next. Worst to first is a lifestyle now.

trade_watch.take: A week ago the model called this a wash; now it's JMoney's first win. Likely's 26.9 led a 50-point rout, Egbuka and Boston added 26.3 from the bench, and Jeanty never even started for Philly before moving on, so Jordan wins this cleanly.

Kai's pair outscored Jefferson 28.8 to 15.8 in the head-to-head debut, exactly as the paper case predicted. But Philly won the game by 35 and moved to 4-1, so Mekhi leads the box score while Alan leads the standings.

The landslide keeps growing: Javonte added a 13.2-point start in another Pillbert win and sits at 42 points since the deal. Diggs didn't play a role for Randy and is stuck at 6, and the fumblers have now lost two straight.

Still zero useful lineup points on either side: Hubbard never cracked Sonny's lineup and scored nothing this week, and Rice remains at zero for Ramon. With the newest ledger entry sending Hubbard on to Alan, this one may end as a trade nobody actually used.

bios.1: Sonny is 4-1 after Bucky Irving's 30.5 carried him past the Habibsters, and his title odds climbed from 11% to 18%. He's still reshaping the roster, with Emanuel Wilson in and a new deal for George Pickens and Ollie Gordon II on the ledger. Week 6 against HULK is the test.
bios.2: Randy has dropped two straight to fall to 3-2, and his title odds sank from 14% to 4%. Jaylen Warren's 33.8 deserved a better result, and the playoff picture is now a coin flip at 48%.
bios.3: Jordan finally has a win, and it was a 50-point beatdown fueled by Isaiah Likely's 26.9 from the Philly trade. At 1-4 with 1% playoff odds, the climb is steep, but the trade haul has already started paying off.
bios.4: Alan has won four straight, posted the week's best score at 143.66, and sits at 4-1 after beating the team he traded with. The model keeps docking him for all the dealmaking, down to 16% title odds, but the scoreboard keeps saying otherwise.
bios.5: Mekhi is 1-4 after leaving 61.56 points on his bench in a 35-point loss to Team Pillbert. His trade haul from Philly outscored Jefferson in their first meeting, and the waiver work never stops, but the lineup calls have to catch up with the roster.
bios.6: Kaushal has the fourth-most points in the league and a 1-4 record to show for it. Puka Nacua gave him 29.2, CeeDee Lamb gave him 1.9, and the two-time champ is hanging on at 30% playoff odds.
bios.7: Ramon's juggernaut is 4-1 with a league-best 695 points and title odds that just jumped to 55%. Josh Allen went for 30.5 while 27 points sat on the bench, which tells you everything about the depth. The commish gets the next crack at slowing it down.
bios.8: Zoe's rookie season hit its first big pothole: a league-low 69.14 that dropped her to 2-3. Goff was the right call at 28.94, but the rest of the lineup didn't follow, and the playoff odds are down to 10%.
